subject: chemistry
question_text: How many sigma and π bonds are present in (a) C₂H₂ (b) C₂H₄?

verification.note: Chapter 3 is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.56-61), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: (a) C₂H₂
lines: Each C−H bond is one σ bond → 2 σ bonds.
The C≡C triple bond is one σ bond and
C₂H₂ has 3 σ bonds and 2 π bonds.
steps.why: In any multiple bond the first bond is a σ bond and every additional bond is a π bond, so the count is read straight off the drawn structure.
common_mistakes: Counting the triple bond as 3 σ bonds. Only the first bond of it is σ; the other two are π.
Forgetting the two C−H bonds in the σ count.
steps.memory_tip: First bond σ, every extra bond π. A triple bond is one σ plus two π.
steps.margin_note: Draw the structure first. The count comes from the picture, not from memory.

steps.label: (b) C₂H₄
lines: The C=C double bond is one σ bond and

lines.text: C₂H₂: 3 σ, 2 π   ·   C₂H₄: 5 σ, 1 π

steps.why: The same first-bond-is-σ rule applied to a double bond: one σ and one π, added to the four C−H σ bonds.
common_mistakes: Writing 4 σ for C₂H₄ by forgetting the C−C σ bond inside the double bond.
steps.memory_tip: Count single lines for σ: four C−H plus one C−C makes five. One line of the double bond is the π.
steps.margin_note: Box both final counts together so neither part is missed in marking.

insider_note: Count from the drawn structure, never from the formula: every single line is one σ bond, and each extra line of a double or triple bond is one π bond.
